text:
Judd Caulfield waited a long time for this. The 25-year-old from Grand Forks, North Dakota, a fifth-round pick by Pittsburgh in 2019, made Anaheim's opening-night roster after a full season with the San Diego Gulls, and NHL.com's Rookie Watch says he's earning the Ducks' trust.

His game is simple and it's working: get to the net. His own chance rate is 1.42 expected goals per 60, a strong number for anyone, and he has four goals, nine points and four power-play points in 16 games. His three-point night against Ottawa (two goals) was the highlight. He's physical too, 56 hits in barely 13 minutes a night.

Some of the points are borrowed. He's shooting 20%, and the Ducks have scored about four more goals than expected with him on the ice, so expect a cooler stretch. Anaheim also gets only 47.6% of the five-on-five expected goals in his minutes, though that's better than the team does without him. Our range has him around 16 goals and 44 points. For a fifth-round rookie at 25, that would be a terrific season.
headline: Judd Caulfield is a late bloomer earning trust
